source_refs.note: Topic 3.1.1, printed page 47 (Figure 3.1, carried by the Lewis bonds original).

blocks.text: According to the Lewis theory, the ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of electrons from an atom with low ionization energy to another atom with high electron affinity. The Na atom (₁₁Na = 2, 8, 1) tends to lose the outermost electron to form Na⁺ (2, 8) ion, which has the electron configuration of ₁₀Ne, a noble gas nearest to it. Chlorine atom Cl (2, 8, 7) gains one electron to form the chloride ion, Cl⁻ (2, 8, 8), also gaining the next noble gas electron arrangement. The oppositely charged Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are held together by strong ionic bond in the crystal of NaCl.
A similar type of bond is expected between group 1 and 2 metals and groups 16 and 17 elements.

blocks.alt: Shell diagrams. A sodium atom (2, 8, 1), electrons as red crosses, and a chlorine atom (2, 8, 7), electrons as green dots; a curved arrow carries sodium's outer electron to chlorine. A thick arrow leads to the bracketed ions: sodium ion [2, 8]+ with its third shell now empty, and chloride ion [2, 8, 8]- whose outer shell holds seven dots and the cross it gained. A box below reads NaCl (Na+Cl-).
blocks.caption: Figure 3.1: Ionic bond formation between Na and Cl (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.1).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the printed Figure 3.1 the sodium ion, labelled [2, 8]⁺, still shows one cross on its third shell, as if it had kept its outer electron. Na⁺ has lost that electron, so its third shell is empty; the figure above shows Na⁺ with the empty shell.
